title: Musher Blueprint Document
description: A composition of one or more components into a single deployable application.
$comment: Structural and type validation only: cross-document reference resolution, slug/directory agreement, and platform capability checks are separate validation layers. See spec.md.

kind.description: Document kind discriminator. Must be BLUEPRINT.

specVersion.description: Version of the Musher specification this document is written against.

BlueprintBinding.$comment: spec.md §4.2 / ADR 0031 §1. The key that is present says where the input’s value comes from: a parameter, another node’s output, or a literal value. Exactly one; `node` goes with `output`. Values from outside the documents enter only through parameters.
BlueprintBinding.description: Where one receiving input’s value comes from.

node.description: Node whose output supplies the value.

BlueprintCompute.description: The compute a workload node runs on: a compute profile, and optional placement pins that narrow where it is placed. Required on a node whose component runs, forbidden on one whose component is EXTERNAL. See spec.md §4.3.

placement.description: Optional pins narrowing the eligible hosts. Absent and a block with no pin set mean the same thing.

profile.$comment: Lookahead-free, so it compiles under RE2 as well as ECMA-262. Only the grammar is here; membership is a capability check (spec.md §4.3).
profile.description: Compute profile slug in family.tier.size form, for example general.standard.small. The profiles actually on offer are published at https://api.musher.dev/v1/reference/compute-profiles.

allOf.$comment: spec.md §4.5 BP-NODE-006. A released claim travels in an identity mode, so viewerClaims requires a viewerIdentity other than NONE.

BlueprintExposure.description: Exposure of one endpoint in the object form: its visibility, whether the platform authenticates viewers, how the workload learns who they are, which of their claims it receives, and which requests pass without a viewer. Bare PUBLIC or PRIVATE is the object form with only visibility.

access.description: Whether the platform authenticates and authorizes a viewer before forwarding: OPEN forwards every request, and AUTHENTICATED admits only viewers the installation's access policy authorizes. PUBLIC only; AUTHENTICATED requires an HTTP, HTTPS or WS endpoint.

accessExemptions.description: Requests an AUTHENTICATED endpoint forwards without a viewer, each one the component declares: PATHS, a request under one of its accessExemptions paths, and BEARER, a request with no viewer session that carries a bearer token.

viewerClaims.description: Facts about the viewer released to the workload beside the subject: EMAIL, the viewer's verified email address, and NAME, their display name. Requires a viewerIdentity other than NONE.

viewerIdentity.description: How the workload learns who the viewer is: NONE; HEADER, a plain request header; ASSERTION, a signed JWT in a request header; or OIDC, the workload signs viewers in as an OpenID Connect client of the platform. Every value but NONE requires access AUTHENTICATED.

visibility.description: Whether the endpoint can be reached from outside the installation.

BlueprintExposure.$comment: spec.md §4.5 / ADR 0034 §1-§2 / ADR 0035 §2, §4. A bare PUBLIC or PRIVATE, or the object form. Bare PUBLIC is { visibility: PUBLIC } with every default: access OPEN, viewerIdentity NONE. Every member but visibility applies only to PUBLIC; an identity mode and accessExemptions require AUTHENTICATED; viewerClaims requires an identity mode (BP-NODE-006).

BlueprintMetadata.description: Identity and description of a blueprint document. The blueprint carries the item’s revision; its sibling listing carries none. See spec.md §3.

description.$comment: spec.md §3 BP-ID-004. Plain text, never rendered as Markdown, bounded like a listing summary. It describes the deployable application to the people who install and operate it; the sibling listing’s summary remains the storefront copy. Structurally optional so a blueprint can be stored while it is being written; BP-ID-005 requires it of a published one.
description.description: What this application is, in one or two plain-text sentences. Required to publish.

revision.description: Item revision: the position of this release in the catalog item's lineage. Orders releases and nothing more.

slug.description: Item slug, which must equal the item's directory name.

allOf.$comment: spec.md §4.1. The form of `componentRef` decides whether a revision is required: a reference beginning ./ or ../ names a document whose own metadata.revision is the revision deployed, so a second one here could contradict it.

bindings.description: Explicit supplier for each receiving input, keyed by the component’s input name.

componentRef.$comment: Both patterns are lookahead-free so they compile under RE2 as well as ECMA-262. A path segment must begin with a letter or digit, which is how `.` and `..` are excluded as interior segments without a negative lookahead; that leaves one spelling per target and keeps the containment check in the semantic phase from having to normalise first.
componentRef.description: Reference to the component document this node deploys, in one of two forms. A repo-local reference begins ./ or ../ and ends .yaml or .yml, and resolves relative to the directory holding this blueprint document; its version is the referenced document's metadata.revision. A published reference is the component's UUID, which names the component across all its revisions, and requires revision to select the one deployed. The relative-path prefix is what tells the two apart: a bare slug is not distinguishable from a UUID.

compute.description: Compute profile and placement for a node whose component runs. Omitted, and forbidden, where the component is EXTERNAL; that agreement is a semantic check against the component (spec.md §4.3).

exposure.description: Exposure of each of the component’s endpoints, keyed by endpoint name; an endpoint left out is PRIVATE. A WORKER endpoint is never PUBLIC.

revision.description: Lineage version pinned by a published reference. Required on a published reference and rejected on a repo-local one, where the referenced document's own metadata.revision supplies it.

volumes.description: Storage allocated to each of the component’s volumes, keyed by the component’s volume name.

BlueprintParameter.$comment: spec.md §5 / ADR 0031 §4 / ADR 0035 §5, §6. A parameter is supplied in one way: submitted (with an optional default), generated, hashed from a generated parameter, or read from outside the documents through `from`. At most one of default, generator, from and hash, and a hash is never offered in a form.
BlueprintParameter.description: Named installation value, bound explicitly by the nodes that consume it.

default.description: Logical default, replaced by a submitted value. No interpolation.

from.description: One whole reference to a value outside the documents: ${{ variables.<path> }} for an organization variable, ${{ connections.<path> }} for an atomic connection, or ${{ deployment.installer.<fact> }} for a fact about the person who created the installation. Never submitted; a connection is replaced whole through acquisition instead.

generator.description: Persisted credential generation; a submitted value is rejected.

hash.description: A hash of a generated parameter, computed once and kept beside it; a submitted value is rejected.

byteLength.description: Number of random bytes generated for the value.

encoding.description: Encoding applied to securely generated random bytes.

BlueprintParameterHash.$comment: spec.md §5.2 BP-PARAM-012 / ADR 0035 §6. The algorithms and their parameters are fixed: BCRYPT is $2b$ with cost 12, and ARGON2ID is m=19456, t=2, p=1 with a 16-byte salt and a 32-byte hash.
BlueprintParameterHash.description: Password hash of a generated parameter.

algorithm.description: BCRYPT ($2b$, cost 12) or ARGON2ID (PHC string, m=19456, t=2, p=1).

BlueprintParameterUi.$comment: spec.md §5.4. The control is derived from the logical schema of the inputs the parameter is bound to rather than declared, so this carries only what a derivation cannot supply.
BlueprintParameterUi.description: Presentation metadata for an install-form parameter.

enumLabels.description: Human-readable label for each enum member, keyed by the member it names. A member left unlabelled is offered as it is spelled.

examples.description: Example values illustrating the form a value takes. Never submitted; parameter.default supplies an omitted submission.

label.description: Human-readable label shown on the install form.

order.description: Relative position of the field within the form. Lower sorts first; a parameter declaring no order sorts after every parameter that declares one.

prominence.description: Standing of the field in the form: PRIMARY is offered directly, SECONDARY behind a disclosure the deploying user opens.

BlueprintPlacement.$comment: Every term pin is a lowercase token rather than a member of a closed set: the grammar is fixed by this contract, the vocabularies are versioned catalog context, not part of this contract (spec.md §4.4). cpuDedication is the exception: two values are the whole concept.
BlueprintPlacement.description: Optional pins that narrow the hosts eligible for the node’s compute profile. A pin never changes the compute the profile names. See spec.md §4.4.

acceleratorInterconnect.description: Required accelerator interconnect, such as nvlink or pcie. Omit to pin nothing. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines; see spec.md §4.4.

acceleratorRuntimes.description: Required accelerator runtimes, such as cuda. An empty array pins nothing, and a term may not repeat. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines; see spec.md §4.4.

acceleratorSKUClass.description: Exact accelerator SKU class to pin. Omit to pin nothing. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines; see spec.md §4.4.

cpuArchitectures.description: Permitted CPU architectures, such as x86_64 or arm64. An empty array pins nothing, and a term may not repeat. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines; see spec.md §4.4.

cpuDedication.description: Whether the node's vCPU must be dedicated rather than shared. Omit to pin nothing. This is the one pin whose vocabulary this contract closes; see spec.md §4.4.

minAcceleratorMemoryGiB.description: Minimum accelerator VRAM in GiB. Omit to pin no floor.

networkClass.description: Required network class. Omit to pin nothing. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines; see spec.md §4.4.

variables.description: Identity and version of each organization variable the installation read.

installationSnapshot.description: Opaque identity and immutable version of the private installation snapshot; never a secret-derived hash.

allOf.$comment: External components have no image, source commit or compute allocation.
External components allocate neither storage nor public exposure.
Git builds pin the source commit as well as the built image digest.

BlueprintSpec.description: Composition, explicit input suppliers, allocation and installation parameters.

components.$comment: spec.md §4 BP-GRAPH-001. Structurally it may be empty so a blueprint can be stored before its first node is chosen, or after its last one is removed; BP-GRAPH-001 requires at least one node of a published blueprint.
components.description: Named component instances. At least one is required to publish.

parameters.description: Every value the installation takes from outside the documents: submitted, generated, organization variables and connections. Nothing binds by name.

BlueprintVersionedIdentity.description: An opaque identity and an immutable version.

minIOPS.description: Minimum provisioned IOPS for this volume. Omit to pin no floor.

sizeGiB.description: Allocated size, at or above the component’s minSizeGiB.

storageClass.description: Required storage class for this volume, such as local-nvme. Omit to pin nothing. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines; see spec.md §4.3.
